title: Trent's band, Lee Hilliard, Godley and the Smiths of Tulsa
summary: He recalls Trent's players Lee Hilliard, A.G. Godley, Henry Smith and his son Geechee Smith, and Bostic and West as peers.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: (Inaudible) Trent I think had one of the greatest bands that ever happened anywhere and he came into Tulsa, and that was one of my favorites. Of course he had that Snubs Mosley and the sliding saxophone, Lee Hilliard--

Let me interrupt you, the first band I went to New York with was Mosley, 1943. Earlier that year I went to New York with Snubs and I joined Basie later and then went to Canada, Chicago, New York, Boston.
Really? I'm glad you mentioned that.
Then they had a young sax sensation, Lee Hilliard and it's sad to say, but Lee was just terrific, but that's one of the musi-
cians that whiskey finally got the best of. Then they had Godley on drums.

And later on when Godley left, Henry Smith, who was the father of Geechee Smith, and his home was in Tulsa and Trent broke up one of those times and so Henry Smith came back to Tulsa and so when he came back to Tulsa he would always--I always seemed to be doing more than any others down there and so I got Henry Smith in the band, and he was the greatest, a very fine drummer, and then we all predicted then his son, he began to play, we predicted he was going to turn out good, and he sure did. Geechee Smith turned out to be a very nice musician and he was one of those high note trumpet players.
Who was this white band that he found there--who was that guy Cherokee?

And of course, who would always be, as the years went on, right at the beginning, you had Earl Bostic and Luther West and they were all there and if anybody could compete with them, they were pretty darn good.
